transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I’m here because I just feel completely drained. Like, even walking from my car into the clinic took a lot out of me, and at work, just opening the EHR feels like it takes everything I have.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends and family?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been too tired to do much, but I haven’t really thought about whether I stopped enjoying things or not.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or have you lost interest in activities you previously found pleasurable?
I’m honestly not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I enjoy things less… I’ve mostly just been feeling too worn out to do much in the first place.
Have you noticed that activities that used to make you happy or give you pleasure don’t do that for you anymore, even if you’re able to do them?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed it that way. I mostly just know I don’t have the energy to do much, so it’s hard to tell if I’m not enjoying things or if I’m just too wiped out to try.
Even when you do manage to do something, like watch a show or talk to a friend, do you find that you don’t really get any enjoyment out of it anymore?

I don’t really know. If I watch something, I’m usually just kind of sitting there, not really paying attention. And with friends, I haven’t thought about whether I’m enjoying it or not. I just feel too drained to tell.

When you do things you used to enjoy, like watching a show or talking to friends, do you find that you don’t feel the same pleasure or happiness from them as you used to, even if you’re able to do them?
I really don’t know. I haven’t noticed a clear difference like that. Most of the time I’m just kind of getting through it, so I can’t tell if it’s less pleasure or if I’m just not really tuned in.
When you’re able to do things you used to enjoy, do you feel less pleasure or satisfaction from them than you used to, even if just a little bit?

I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to it like that. I know I feel kind of worn out when I do things, but I can’t say for sure if it’s less pleasure or just me not being fully there.
Can you think back to a time before you started feeling this way—did you used to enjoy activities more, like watching a show or spending time with friends, compared to how you feel about them now?

I don’t really know. I mean, I guess before this I probably did things more normally, but I can’t clearly compare it. Right now I just feel kind of disconnected from it, so I’m not sure if I enjoyed it more before or if I’m just not thinking about it the same way.
Looking back, would you say that you used to enjoy activities like watching a show or spending time with friends more in the past compared to how you feel about them now?

I still can’t really say. Maybe I did, but I don’t remember it clearly enough to compare. Right now it’s just hard for me to tell if I’m enjoying things less or if I’m just not paying attention to it the same way.
Looking back, is there anything you used to do that you know you enjoyed, even if you don’t do it much anymore?
I’m not sure. Nothing really comes to mind that I can say for sure, like “yeah, I definitely enjoyed that.” I know I used to do normal stuff, but I can’t pin down one thing right now.
Can you think of any specific activity or thing you used to do regularly that you looked forward to or felt good doing, even if you do it less now?
I honestly can’t think of anything specific. I know I had routines and stuff I did, but nothing stands out as something I really looked forward to or felt good doing. It’s hard to say.
Looking back at the last few months, have you noticed that you don’t get as much pleasure or satisfaction out of activities as you used to, even ones you used to enjoy?

I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed it clearly one way or the other. I guess I’m not paying close enough attention to whether I’m enjoying things or not, so I can’t honestly say it’s less than before.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt that you’ve had less energy than usual or felt more tired than usual, even after resting?

Yeah. I feel completely drained lately. Even after I rest, it’s like my body still doesn’t have anything in it. Just walking from my car to here, or even opening the EHR at work, feels like it takes everything I’ve got.
Looking back, have you found that you’re less interested in things overall, even if just a little, compared to how you felt a few months ago?
I’m not really sure. I can’t say I’ve clearly noticed being less interested overall. Mostly I just feel worn out, so it’s hard to tell if it’s interest or just not having the energy.
Over the past few weeks, have you felt down, sad, or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah… most days, I’d say. After my energy dropped so much, I started feeling really empty and hopeless. Like I already messed up my future in healthcare before it even really got started.
Have you felt like you’re a failure or that you’ve let others down more than usual lately?

Yeah. I keep feeling like I’m messing everything up. At work I replay every chart I touched and every set of vitals I took, over and over, thinking maybe I hurt someone or missed something… even when my supervisors say nothing bad happened. It just feels like I let people down.
Have you noticed that it's harder for you to think clearly, focus, or make decisions lately?

Yeah, definitely. When I was trying to chart, I couldn’t stay with it. Like every hallway noise, every phone ringing, or someone moving outside the door would pull my attention away, and then I’d look back and forget what patient I was even documenting.
Looking back, would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to care about, even things that were important to you?

I’m not sure I’d say completely. I mean, I haven’t really been into things the same way, but I don’t know if it’s like I totally lost interest in everything. It’s more like… I just don’t have much in me for anything right now.
